cues.t: Before the beginning,
before the mountains were raised,
or ever the earth and the world were formed,
there was God.
And He, the Father of Spirits,
conceived of our existence
from before the foundation of the world,
He knew us. And so he moved to create us,
to fellowship with Him and with one another.
In the beginning was the Word,
and the Word was with God,
and the Word was God.
The same was in the beginning with God.
All things were made by Him,
and without Him was not anything
made that was made.
In the Word was life, and that life
was the light of men.
His light shineth
in darkness, and the darkness
comprehended it not.
The Word of God spoke the heavens
and the earth into being.
[ ♫ music ♫ ]
But the earth was without form and void.
Darkness was upon the face of the deep.
[ ♫ music ♫ ]
The Spirit of God
moved upon the face of the waters.
He said, “Let there be light.”
And He divided
the light from the darkness, saying,
“Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters
to divide the waters
from the waters.” And God called the firmament heaven.
[ ♫ music ♫ ]
God spoke again, “Let the waters
be gathered into one place,
and let the dry land appear.”
And God called the dry land earth.
The gathering together of the waters
called He seas.
God, the Father of Spirits,
gathered a Divine Council
of heavenly beings.
He described the day.
“When I laid the foundations of the earth.
The morning stars sang together,
and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”
The first among them was the WORD,
the First Born of every creature,
the express image of the Father.
This same Word would be born
as Jesus of Nazareth.
The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.
He was in the world,
and the world was made by Him,
and the world knew Him not.
Of the Father are all things.
And by the Son in heaven
and in earth, visible and invisible,
all things were created by Him, and for Him,
and by Him all things consist.
He is before all things
the Heir of all things,
by whom God the Father made the worlds.
The Word commanded,
“Let there be lights in the firmament
of the heaven to divide day from night.
Let them be for signs
and for seasons, for days and for years.”
Two lights were made to shine.
The greater light to rule the day and the lesser
light to rule the night.
He made the stars also.
God did not create the earth in vain.
He formed it to be inhabited.
The Word spoke again.
“Let the waters bring forth
abundantly the moving creature that hath life:
great whales, and every living
creature that moves,
which the waters brought forth abundantly.”
“Let the earth bring forth
grass, the herb yielding seed, and the tree
yielding fruit.” And God
blessed them all, saying,
“Be fruitful and multiply,
and fill the waters in the seas.”
“Let the earth
bring forth living creatures, the cattle,
and creeping things,
and beasts of the earth, and fowl
that may fly above the earth
in the open firmament of heaven.
Let them multiply upon the earth.”
Then God the Father said
to the Divine council,
“Let us make man in Our image,
after Our likeness, male and female.”
He formed man of the dust of the ground,
and breathed into him the breath of life.
And man became a living soul.
And God planted a garden eastward in Eden.
And there he put the man
whom he had formed to dress it
and to keep it.
The father said, “It is not good
that the man should be alone.”
So He made a woman
and brought her unto the man,
explaining, “Therefore
shall a man cleave unto his wife,
and they shall be one flesh.”
And God commanded,
“Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over
the fowl of the air, and over the cattle,
and over all the earth,
and over every creeping thing
upon the earth.” God blessed them, and said
unto them,
“Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish
the earth, and subdue it,
and have dominion over all life.”
Thus the heavens
and the earth were finished,
and all the host of them. And God
looked upon everything that He had made.
And behold, it was very good.
The invisible God could be known
through the visible creation.
Then God rested from all his work which He created
and made.
God knew beforehand
that Eden would not last, that humankind
would be deceived, tempted, sin, and fall
from the presence of God to mortality.
Still, the father had chosen us in him
before the foundation of the world.
The dramatic events
that took place in the garden led to the conditions
of mortality and opposition in all things.
It was by God's plan that creation
and the state of humankind
was brought to their present state.
After Adam's transgression.
God addressed the council.
“Behold, mankind
has become as one of us to know
good and evil.”
Then the Father asked, “Who shall I send?
Who among you is willing to maintain
the holy demands of justice
while offering atoning
mercy and divine grace?”
The Word saw that there was no one,
and marveled that there was no intercessor.
So by His own arm mankind must be saved.
He volunteered to be the Lamb,
slain from the foundation of the world.
He was for ordained and anointed by God
the Father before the foundation of the world,
to be the Messiah who would show mankind
the way and redeem souls unto the Father.
The Word who created heaven and earth,
Jehovah of the Old Testament,
was the same God that would be born
as Jesus of Nazareth,
the Savior and Redeemer of the world.
Before
withdrawing His presence from the children
He had created,
God made coats of skins of animals to clothe them.
He gave them instructions
and sent them forth from
Eden to till the ground
from whence mankind was taken.
The Word
came to Adam,
“In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread,
till thou return unto the ground.
For out of it was thou taken.
For dust thou art, and unto dust
shalt thou return.”
Most important of all these events,
God promised eventual victory over evil
and the fall of mankind.
Adam was comforted
by the promise of eternal life God made from
before the world began, knowing God
cannot lie.
By Divine Will we experience desire,
hardship, sorrow,
temptations, enmity, labor, and death.
But this is not all
we were also meant to know
fulfillment, comfort, joy,
holy inspiration, love, rest,
and life. For each of these life
experiences carries its opposite
that we might know the one by the other.
Adam taught his posterity
of God's promises of salvation from evil,
and redemption from the fall
from God's presence.
From that time, men
began to call upon the name of the Lord.
Their faith and hope were expressed
through prayer, worship,
and through sacrifices that foreshadowed
the atoning sacrifice
of the promised Messiah.
The Great Patriarchs and Prophets
knew these things since the world began.
Each of them learning to walk with God.
For the Spirit of Christ, which was in them,
testified before hand
of the sufferings of Christ, and the glory
that should follow those
that do His commandments.
For they will have the right
to the Tree of Life
restored to them as they enter
through the gates into
the Kingdom of Heaven.
Oh, God.
We lift our eyes to
the work of your fingers.
The moon and the stars
you set in their places.
And the heavens declare your glory.
The skies proclaim the work of your hands.
Day after day they shout their witness.
Night after night they reveal knowledge.
Without speech.
Without words. Without a sound.
Their voice still carries
to the ends of the earth.
And so we come before You and wonder...
Through your Beloved Son,
You made all this, and us.
You are the Divine Shepherd
of the starry host,
calling each of them by name
and by Your great power,
Not one of them is missing.
By Your word the heavens were made,
and all their host
by the breath of Your mouth.
When You laid the foundations, the Morning Stars
sang together, and the Children
of God shouted for joy.
All things bear
witness of You. The earth
and everything upon it.
Its motion and the planets
moving in their fixed courses.
The earth turns upon her wings.
The sun gives light by day, the moon by night.
And the stars shine
as they move in their glory.
And in even the least of these, we have seen
You moving in majesty and power.
We thank You
that nothing You have made
is without its witness.
The animals teach us of You.
The birds of the sky tell of You.
The earth instructs us,
and the fish of the sea
declare the work of Your hand.
For which of them does not know
that Your hand has done this?
All things You have made
bear witness of You.
Things in the heavens above,
things upon the earth,
things beneath. All of them testify of You.
Everything You have given points to You.
And in the fullness of it all
we behold Your Son,
through whom all things were made.
He came to us as an offering,
a sacrifice to save and redeem the world.
And into all this vastness,
You still turn Your face toward us.
What are we that You keep us in mind?
What are mortal children
that You care for us?
Yet You have made us a little lower than the angels,
and crowned us with glory and honor.
You have given us charge
over the works of Your hands
and entrusted the earth to our care.
You created us in Your own image
and called us Your own.
For this we have no worthy words,
only thanks.
Your glory is plain.
Oh, Father, let us never fail to see it.
Since the world was made, Your unseen
qualities, Your eternal power,
Your very nature have been plain
in the things You have made.
And we will not turn our eyes away.
So we confess Your hand in all things,
and withhold nothing from Your will.
All creation answers You,
and we answer with it.
Let the sun and moon praise You.
Let all the shining stars praise You.
Let them praise Your name.
For at Your command they were created.
The hills break forth and singing before You.
And all the trees of the field
clap their hands for joy.
God our Father, how majestic
is Your name in all the earth.
Send us from this place with eyes
open to Your glory, hearts
humbled by Your goodness, and hands
willing to care for all You have made.
We offer this prayer in the name of
Your Son, Jesus Christ.
Amen.
